body: Three internal inconsistencies undermine the evaluation design. (1) The human-annotation requirement is self-contradictory: FR-001 demands human feasibility scores for all 1000 prompts, while FR-009 requires only 200; FR-010 then bars synthetic scores from evaluation, so under the FR-009 budget the paired tests in FR-005 would rest on a 200-prompt subset while the power analysis in the Assumptions assumes n=1000 — the stated power of ≥0.8 does not transfer to n=200. (2) US-3's acceptance scenario 3 ('the analysis confirms that the improvement is not due to chance (p < 0.05)') builds the hypothesized result into the acceptance criteria; a spec should require the test be run and reported, not that it succeed. (3) The 'Alignment Score' entity is defined as a correlation, which is a property of a set of samples, yet US-1 requires a per-row 'alignment delta' per prompt — a per-prompt alignment score is never operationally defined (verifier score minus human score? verifier score alone?). Additionally, the motivation claims the target is 'implicit contradictions,' but US-2's contradiction detection is 'antonym matching' on explicit cases like 'Make the sky blue and keep it dark' — the mechanism demonstrated in the spec addresses only the explicit subset, and no acceptance scenario covers implicit conflicts. Finally, the source of 'human-annotated feasibility scores' for a downloaded public dataset (FR-001) is unspecified; crowd-sourcing per FR-009 covers at most 200 prompts, leaving the provenance of the remaining 800 annotations unestablished.
